snapshot_note: v0.53.0 released on develop 2026-07-26 - `-static-libmadc` now works in the .o LINK lane, lifting forest-carriers S5's last stated boundary. The AOT ledger is carried as MIR modules, so the pieces a program needs are pulled into a PRIVATE object-mode context, generated, emitted with MIR_gen_object_emit, and merged into the same builder as the .o inputs. Through the merge deliberately: a builder's symbol table is append-only (MIR_object_add_symbol never dedupes by name), and the unification that turns the inputs' UNDEF entries into references to the runtime's definitions IS the merge - so the runtime rides the ONE unification implementation, on the read-back path both containers (ELF ET_REL and MH_OBJECT) already gate. No new format code, no fork change. Generalized rather than duplicated: cir_ledger_pull takes a SEED list (the builder's UNDEF names join the module imports under the same not-defined filter), and the cover analysis takes the reference LIST rather than its source (source lanes pass context imports, the .o lane passes MIR_object_undef_name) - same classifier, same two diagnostics. Fixed on the way: the AOT-ledger carrier now opens HEADER-ONLY (the ledger is a container-global segment, but the probe ran complete_open, which binds the frozen string pool and arena into LIVE parse state - it died with 'forest thaw requires a live string pool' in a lane with no lexer). New -fno-eval-shims: every .o carries __madc_shim_* host-call adapters whose twelve madc_value_* imports are Tier B, an executable emit from source skips them and a .o cannot know, so the build says it (the -fPIC shape). Fork unchanged (1.0-madc.0.52.0 @ba216dea).

ADDENDUM — cctype:111 ROOT CAUSE FOUND (fix NOT written; this is the top NEXT item). It is NOT a libc++ problem and NOT an include problem: it is a C++ PARSER bug, reducible to EIGHT LINES with no library headers. `template <class T, class U> struct cmp<T, U, typename vt<decltype(declval<T>() < declval<U>())>::type> {};` — madc says 'Unexpected end of data', g++ and clang print `1 0`. The `<` in `declval<T>() < declval<U>()` is a LESS-THAN OPERATOR, but the scanner reading the partial specialization's template-argument list treats it as opening a nested argument list, consumes declval<U>'s `>` as the closer, and runs to EOF. THE CASCADE, and it is worth understanding before touching anything: libc++'s __utility/is_pointer_in_range.h contains exactly that construct. It dies mid-header, so its _LIBCPP_BEGIN_NAMESPACE_STD never opens a namespace — and the matching _LIBCPP_END_NAMESPACE_STD then CLOSES SCOPES THAT WERE NEVER OPENED. From there the scope stack is wrong, later global declarations (glibc's isalnum among them) are unreachable from ::, and `using ::isalnum;` fails at cctype:111 SIX HEADERS DOWNSTREAM of the actual defect. Every order-dependence in my earlier bisects was just which header first drags in is_pointer_in_range.h. THE CORRECT RULE IS ALREADY IMPLEMENTED, IN ONE PLACE: parser.cpp:38774 tracks angle brackets ONLY outside parens/subscripts, and its comment cites this exact shape (decltype(forward<_Tp>(t) < forward<_Up>(u))) together with the same consumed-to-EOF symptom. A SIBLING scanner lacks the guard. There are SIX angle_depth scanners (parser.cpp:3320 collect_template_argument_spelling [has paren_depth], 18083/18104 spelling helpers, 38358 collect_template_default_argument, 38716 [the fixed reference], 45465 skip_template_suffix_tokens, 48445). SIX COPIES OF ONE RULE IS THE REAL FINDING — the fix is to make them SHARE it, not to add the guard a seventh time (design-principles.md, no-parallel-implementations.md).
